chunks: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Jaʿfar, that ʿAlī عليه السلام used to say:

If the muhrim slaughters game outside the Haram, then it is carrion; neither one who is non-muhrim nor a muhrim may eat it. And if the non-muhrim slaughters game within the interior of the Haram, then it is carrion; neither one who is non-muhrim nor a muhrim may eat it.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: the sacred sanctuary in which special hunting restrictions apply
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: a person in the state of ihram
key_terms.مَيْتَةٌ: carrion, an unlawfully dead animal not permitted for consumption
key_terms.مُحِلٌّ: a person not in the state of ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on game slaughtered by a muhrim or inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that game slaughtered unlawfully in connection with ihram or the sanctuary of the Haram is treated as maytah and is not lawful to eat. It establishes that both the state of ihram and the sanctity of the Haram affect the permissibility of hunted game.
